---
title: Keyword System — Provoke, Ranged, Flying, Dying Wish, Opening Gambit
type: spec
status: draft
tags: [game-design, keywords, combat, units, rust]
---

## Overview

Define the core keyword system for units, inspired by Duelyst's modifier system but scoped to 5 keywords that create tactical depth. Keywords are boolean flags on GridUnit that modify how the unit interacts with movement, attacks, and death. Designed as the minimal viable set — expandable later but complete enough for tactical variety.

## Locked Decisions

- D1: **Keyword as enum flags** — Keywords are an enum `Keyword { Provoke, Ranged, Flying, DyingWish(Effect), OpeningGambit(Effect) }` stored as `Vec<Keyword>` on GridUnit. DyingWish and OpeningGambit carry an Effect that triggers on the respective event.
- D2: **5 core keywords** — Provoke, Ranged, Flying, Dying Wish, Opening Gambit. Each targets a different tactical axis: positioning (Provoke), threat range (Ranged), mobility (Flying), death value (DW), summon value (OG).
- D3: **No keyword interactions** — Keywords are independent. No keyword references another keyword in its implementation. This prevents combinatorial complexity.
- D4: **Keywords are per-unit, not per-card** — A unit's keywords are defined on its GridUnitTemplate (used in Summon cards) or as inherent properties of hero/enemy types.

## Requirements

### Functional Requirements

- FR-1: Keyword enum: `Provoke`, `Ranged`, `Flying`, `DyingWish(Effect)`, `OpeningGambit(Effect)`. Stored as `Vec<Keyword>` in GridUnit.
- FR-2: **Provoke** — Enemy units cannot move through tiles adjacent to a Provoke unit. BFS pathfinding treats Provoke-adjacent tiles as blocked (unless the moving unit is Flying). If a unit starts its turn adjacent to a Provoke unit, it must attack the Provoke unit if it attacks at all (forced target).
- FR-2a: Provoke forced-target only applies if the Provoke unit is in attack range.
- FR-2b: Multiple Provoke units: the attacking unit may choose which to attack.
- FR-3: **Ranged** — Unit's `attack_range` is effectively full board (99). Ranged units can attack any tile on the grid regardless of distance. Movement range is unaffected.
- FR-3a: Ranged units do not counterattack when attacked (they have no melee reach). Exception: if the attacker is adjacent, the Ranged unit CAN counterattack (point-blank rule).
- FR-3b: Ranged unit's attack is blocked by enemy units in the line of fire (obstruction). Check if any occupied tile lies on the straight line between attacker and target. If so, the attack is blocked unless the attacker or target has Flying.
- FR-4: **Flying** — Unit can pass over any tile type and any unit (friend or foe) during movement. BFS treats all tiles as passable (cost 1). Flying units ignore Provoke adjacency blocking.
- FR-4a: Flying does not affect attack range or targeting — only movement.
- FR-5: **Dying Wish** — Effect triggers when the unit dies (HP ≤ 0, removed from grid). The effect resolves at the unit's position before removal. Effect types: Damage, Heal, Shield, Summon (spawn a unit).
- FR-5a: Dying Wish resolves before the unit is visually removed (death animation plays after).
- FR-6: **Opening Gambit** — Effect triggers immediately when the unit is summoned (placed on grid). Fire before summoning sickness is applied. Effect types: Damage, Heal, Shield, DrawCards.
- FR-6a: Opening Gambit targeting: can target any valid tile within range of the spawn position.
- FR-7: Keywords are defined on GridUnitTemplate and copied to the spawned GridUnit. Hero and enemy types define their keywords in constants.
- FR-8: Effect resolution for DyingWish/OpeningGambit uses the same `resolve_effect()` function as card effects.

### Non-Functional Requirements

- NFR-1: Keyword logic is pure Rust (zero Godot deps), unit-testable.
- NFR-2: BFS with Provoke/Flying checks must complete in < 1ms (only adds adjacency check per step).
- NFR-3: Ranged obstruction check: O(n) where n = max(BOARDCOL, BOARDROW) — negligible for 9×5.
- NFR-4: No keyword references another keyword in its implementation.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1: Keyword enum defined with 5 variants (Provoke, Ranged, Flying, DyingWish, OpeningGambit)
- [ ] AC-2: GridUnit stores `Vec<Keyword>`, copied from template on spawn
- [ ] AC-3: Provoke unit blocks enemy movement through its adjacent tiles
- [ ] AC-4: Flying unit passes over Provoke adjacency and any unit-occupied tiles
- [ ] AC-5: Unit adjacent to Provoke must attack it if attacking at all
- [ ] AC-6: Ranged unit can attack any tile on the grid
- [ ] AC-7: Ranged unit does NOT counterattack when attacked from range (does counterattack when attacked melee-adjacent)
- [ ] AC-8: Ranged attack blocked by enemy unit obstruction in line of fire
- [ ] AC-9: Flying ignores obstruction for Ranged attacks
- [ ] AC-10: Dying Wish effect triggers on unit death at its position
- [ ] AC-11: Opening Gambit effect triggers on summon before summoning sickness
- [ ] AC-12: Dying Wish / Opening Gambit use existing resolve_effect() function
- [ ] AC-13: BFS pathfinding accounts for Provoke adjacency blocking
- [ ] AC-14: All existing tests plus new keyword-specific tests pass with `cargo test`

## Scenarios

### Scenario 1: Provoke Blocks Movement
**Given** enemy unit positions at (3, 2), Provoke unit at (4, 2), and player hero at (2, 2)
**When** the enemy tries to path from (3, 2) to (5, 2) (past the Provoke unit)
**Then** BFS reports (4, 2) as blocked (adjacent to Provoke)
**Then** the enemy must find an alternate path or cannot pass

### Scenario 2: Flying Ignores Provoke
**Given** Flying unit at (3, 2), Provoke unit at (4, 2)
**When** the Flying unit moves from (3, 2) to (5, 2)
**Then** BFS allows passing through tile (4, 2) (Flying ignores Provoke)
**Then** the Flying unit completes its movement past the Provoke unit

### Scenario 3: Ranged Attack with Obstruction
**Given** Ranged hero at (0, 2), enemy unit at (3, 2), blocking enemy at (2, 2)
**When** hero tries to attack enemy at (3, 2)
**Then** the attack is blocked by enemy at (2, 2) (obstruction)
**When** the blocking enemy moves away
**Then** hero can attack (3, 2) directly

### Scenario 4: Dying Wish Triggers
**Given** a minion with DyingWish(Damage(2)) has 1 HP remaining
**When** the minion takes 3 damage (HP → 0)
**Then** the Dying Wish resolves: Damage(2) is dealt to all units within AoE 1 of the minion's position
**Then** the minion is removed from the grid

### Scenario 5: Opening Gambit Triggers on Summon
**Given** a Summon card for a unit with OpeningGambit(Heal(3))
**When** the card is played and the unit appears on the grid
**Then** the Opening Gambit fires: Heal(3) targets the nearest damaged friendly unit
**Then** summoning sickness is applied to the unit

## Technical Notes

- Keyword enum: added to `rust/src/core/grid/model/unit.rs`. GridUnit gains `keywords: Vec<Keyword>` field.
- Provoke: BFS in `movement.rs` adds an adjacency check: `if tile has Provoke unit && moving unit does NOT have Flying, block step into tiles adjacent to the Provoke unit`.
- Provoke forced-target: attack validation in `engine.rs::player_attack()` checks if any adjacent enemy has Provoke. If so, one of them must be the attack target.
- Ranged: `attack_range` set to 99 in unit template. `can_attack(from, to, state)` checks range value instead of hardcoded adjacency.
- Ranged counterattack: `base_attack.rs` checks if defender has Ranged and attacker is not adjacent — skip counterattack.
- Ranged obstruction: `fn line_of_sight(from, to, state) -> bool` — Bresenham line check between from and to; returns false if any occupied tile blocks.
- Flying: BFS in `movement.rs` — Flying units traverse all tiles at cost 1, no blocking checks.
- Dying Wish: `engine.rs::apply_damage()` or `die()` function — after setting alive=false, check if unit has DyingWish keyword, call resolve_effect with stored effect.
- Opening Gambit: `spawn.rs::spawn_unit()` — after placing the unit on grid, before applying summoning sickness, check for OpeningGambit, resolve effect.
- All effect-holding keywords (DyingWish, OpeningGambit) store a serialized Effect. JSON-compatible for save/load.

## Open Questions

- [ ] OQ-1: **(RESOLVED)** Provoke blocks only movement through adjacent tiles, not attack targeting. Units can still attack past a Provoke unit (only Ranged units need LOS).
- [ ] OQ-2: **(RESOLVED)** Ranged counterattack: none at range, yes at adjacency. This matches Duelyst and prevents Ranged from being too strong in melee.
- [ ] OQ-3: **(RESOLVED)** Line of sight for Ranged: Bresenham straight-line only. No curved or multi-tile LOS. Simple and sufficient for 9×5.
- [ ] OQ-4: Which units get which keywords in Phase 1? Hero starts with no keywords. Enemies: Easy (none), Medium (Provoke or Ranged), Hard (Provoke + Ranged or Dying Wish). Summon cards define keywords per unit template.

## Overview

Define the core keyword system for units, inspired by Duelyst's modifier system. Keywords modify how a unit interacts with movement, attacks, and death. **Ranged is not a keyword** — it's the `Range::Ranged` variant on the unified `Range` enum shared between units and cards (see `wiki:specs:card-system-in-battle-deck`). Scoped to 4 core keywords that create tactical depth.

## Locked Decisions

- D1: **Keyword as enum** — `Keyword { Provoke, Flying, DyingWish(Effect), OpeningGambit(Effect) }` stored as `Vec<Keyword>` on GridUnit. Ranged is the `Range::Ranged` enum variant, not a keyword.
- D2: **4 core keywords** — Provoke, Flying, Dying Wish, Opening Gambit. Each targets a different tactical axis: positioning (Provoke), mobility (Flying), death value (DW), summon value (OG).
- D3: **No keyword interactions** — Keywords are independent. No keyword references another keyword in its implementation. This prevents combinatorial complexity.
- D4: **Keywords are per-unit, not per-card** — A unit's keywords are defined on its GridUnitTemplate (used in Summon cards) or as inherent properties of hero/enemy types.

## Requirements

### Functional Requirements

- FR-1: Keyword enum: `Provoke`, `Flying`, `DyingWish(Effect)`, `OpeningGambit(Effect)`. Stored as `Vec<Keyword>` in GridUnit.
- FR-2: **Provoke** — Enemy units cannot move through tiles adjacent to a Provoke unit. BFS pathfinding treats tiles Chebyshev-adjacent to a Provoke unit as blocked (unless the moving unit is Flying). If a unit starts its turn adjacent to a Provoke unit and that Provoke unit is in attack range, the unit must attack the Provoke unit if it attacks at all (forced target).
- FR-2a: Multiple adjacent Provoke units: attacking unit may choose which Provoke unit to target.
- FR-3: **Flying** — Unit can pass over any tile type and any unit (friend or foe) during movement. BFS treats all tiles as passable (cost 1). Flying units ignore Provoke adjacency blocking entirely.
- FR-3a: Flying does not affect attack range or targeting — only movement and Provoke immunity.
- FR-4: **Dying Wish** — Effect triggers when the unit dies (HP ≤ 0, removed from grid). The effect resolves at the unit's position before removal. Effect types: Damage, Heal, Shield, Summon.
- FR-4a: Dying Wish resolves before the unit is visually removed (death animation plays after).
- FR-5: **Opening Gambit** — Effect triggers immediately when the unit is summoned (placed on grid). Fires before summoning sickness is applied. Effect types: Damage, Heal, Shield, DrawCards.
- FR-5a: Opening Gambit targeting follows standard card targeting rules (Range + TargetFilter + AoE).
- FR-6: Keywords are defined on GridUnitTemplate and copied to the spawned GridUnit. Hero and enemy types define their keywords in constants.
- FR-7: Effect resolution for DyingWish/OpeningGambit uses the same `resolve_effect()` function as card effects.

### Non-Functional Requirements

- NFR-1: Keyword logic is pure Rust (zero Godot deps), unit-testable.
- NFR-2: BFS with Provoke/Flying checks must complete in < 1ms.
- NFR-3: No keyword references another keyword in its implementation.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1: Keyword enum defined with 4 variants (Provoke, Flying, DyingWish, OpeningGambit)
- [ ] AC-2: Ranged is NOT in the Keyword enum (it's Range::Ranged on GridUnit instead)
- [ ] AC-3: GridUnit stores `Vec<Keyword>`, copied from template on spawn
- [ ] AC-4: Provoke unit blocks enemy movement through its adjacent tiles
- [ ] AC-5: Flying unit passes over Provoke adjacency and any unit-occupied tiles
- [ ] AC-6: Unit adjacent to Provoke must attack it if attacking at all
- [ ] AC-7: Dying Wish effect triggers on unit death at its position
- [ ] AC-8: Opening Gambit effect triggers on summon before summoning sickness
- [ ] AC-9: Dying Wish / Opening Gambit use existing resolve_effect() function
- [ ] AC-10: BFS pathfinding accounts for Provoke adjacency blocking
- [ ] AC-11: All tests pass with `cargo test`

## Scenarios

### Scenario 1: Provoke Blocks Movement
**Given** enemy unit at (3, 2), Provoke unit at (4, 2), hero at (2, 2)
**When** the enemy tries to path from (3, 2) to (5, 2) (past the Provoke unit)
**Then** BFS reports (4, 2) as blocked (adjacent to Provoke unit)
**Then** the enemy must find an alternate path or cannot pass

### Scenario 2: Flying Ignores Provoke
**Given** Flying unit at (3, 2), Provoke unit at (4, 2)
**When** the Flying unit moves from (3, 2) to (5, 2)
**Then** BFS allows passing through (4, 2) (Flying ignores Provoke)
**Then** the Flying unit completes its movement past the Provoke unit

### Scenario 3: Dying Wish Triggers
**Given** a minion with DyingWish(Damage(2)) has 1 HP remaining
**When** the minion takes 3 damage (HP → 0)
**Then** the Dying Wish resolves: Damage 2 to all units within AoE::Single at the minion's position
**Then** the minion is removed from the grid

### Scenario 4: Opening Gambit on Summon
**Given** a Summon card for a unit with OpeningGambit(Heal(3))
**When** the card is played and the unit appears on the grid
**Then** the Opening Gambit fires: Heal(3) targets the nearest damaged friendly unit
**Then** summoning sickness is applied to the unit

### Scenario 5: Provoke Forced Target
**Given** hero is adjacent to a Provoke enemy and also adjacent to a non-Provoke enemy
**When** the hero tries to attack the non-Provoke enemy
**Then** the attack is rejected — "Must attack Provoke unit"
**When** the hero attacks the Provoke enemy instead
**Then** the attack succeeds

## Technical Notes

- Keyword enum: added to `rust/src/core/grid/model/unit.rs`. GridUnit gains `keywords: Vec<Keyword>` field.
- Provoke BFS: in `movement.rs`, for each step candidate, check if that tile is Chebyshev-adjacent to any unit with Provoke keyword. If so and moving unit does NOT have Flying, block the step.
- Provoke forced-target: `engine.rs::player_attack()` checks if any adjacent enemy has Provoke keyword. If so, the attack target must be one of those units.
- Flying: BFS in `movement.rs` — Flying units traverse all tiles at cost 1, no blocking checks.
- Dying Wish: in `die()` or `apply_damage()` — after setting alive=false, check keywords for DyingWish, call resolve_effect with stored effect at unit's position.
- Opening Gambit: in `spawn_unit()` — after placing unit on grid, before applying summoning sickness, check for OpeningGambit, resolve effect.
- Ranged is NOT a keyword: instead, a unit has `range: Range` field. `Range::Ranged` on GridUnit provides full-board attack range and unconditional counterattack. See `wiki:specs:card-system-in-battle-deck` for Range enum, `wiki:specs:enemy-system-deck-ai-difficulty` for unit combat.

## Open Questions

- [ ] OQ-1: **(RESOLVED)** Ranged removed from keywords — it's `Range::Ranged` on the shared Range enum.
- [ ] OQ-2: **(RESOLVED)** Provoke forced-target only if Provoke unit is in attack range.
- [ ] OQ-3: **(RESOLVED)** No keyword interactions — each keyword is independent.
- [ ] OQ-4: Which units get which keywords in Phase 1? Hero starts with none. Enemies: Easy (none), Medium (Provoke), Hard (Provoke + Flying or Dying Wish). Summon cards define keywords per minion template.
